headline: 86 Dogs Rescued From Missouri Breeders in 'Operation Eclipse'
meta_description: Animal Rescue Corps and National Mill Dog Rescue freed 86 dogs from commercial breeders across southern Missouri counties in coordinated mission.
summary_short: 86 dogs ranging from 7 weeks to 9 years old were surrendered from commercial breeders across southern Missouri in a coordinated rescue effort.
body:
Animal Rescue Corps and National Mill Dog Rescue coordinated a rescue mission on August 27 that freed 86 dogs surrendered from commercial breeders across several southern Missouri counties. The operation, named "Operation Eclipse" to mark the lunar eclipse, brought together dogs of many breeds that had lived in breeding operations.

The rescued animals included poodles, mini Australian shepherds, doodles, dachshunds, and English bulldogs—spanning a wide age range from puppies as young as 7 weeks to senior dogs around 8 or 9 years old. This diversity reflected the scope of the breeders involved across the region.

The dogs were transported to Animal Rescue Corps' rescue center, where they could begin their recovery and transition to permanent homes. The mission demonstrated how coordinated animal rescue efforts can address the welfare concerns surrounding commercial breeding operations.
